title: Aggregation View
description:
For bus systems as CAN, LIN, FlexRay and others messages transport signals,
which typically follow a "last is best" semantics.

For this reason it common to have a live view that updates with the
last messages to see the latest values of the signals.

This patch implements such an aggregation view for live capturing.

Signed-off-by: Dr. Lars Völker <lars.voelker@technica-engineering.de>

notes.body: @giovanni.musto this might be interesting for you
Definitely
I thought so :-)
So what is an "aggregation view"?

Let's assume you are capturing an Ethernet link and you want to just see the newest packet of each local device in the network. You would set the filter to "eth.src" and activate the aggregation view. This would just show in the regular Wireshark while capturing only a single line per "eth.src"; thus, aggregating them with "last is best" semantics.

While for Ethernet this might not make a lot of sense in some cases, for field bus systems like CAN, LIN, or FlexRay, this makes so much sense that most tools support a view like this.

Let's assume on CAN, you have a message that includes vehicle speed and another message that includes Acceleration Pedal position. You could now configure that the messages are aggregated based on the CAN ID and filter for the messages you need. While you would be doing a live capture, you would only see those messages being updated.

Does this help?

So is it a "show only the *last* - i.e., most recent - packet that matches a packet-matching expression" view?

From

> Let's assume on CAN, you have a message that includes vehicle speed and another message that includes Acceleration Pedal position. You could now configure that the messages are aggregated based on the CAN ID and filter for the messages you need. While you would be doing a live capture, you would only see those messages being updated.

it sounds as if it might be more complicated than that - would it show the most recent CAN message of each of the types that match the filter, so you'd see the most recent vehicle speed message *and* the most recent acceleration pedal position message?
Yes, it show the most recent packet per value of the filter. So, if use "eth.src" and see 3 different source address, you see the latest packet of each. This results in 3 resulting packets.
Yes, sorry. It is a field. We called it "aggregation fields" in the config.

This commit appears to have broken the saving of settings in **Preferences** -> **Expert** (unless I'm mistaken).

At commit 4944932c2474a4df3140c039ad1c13f0871acdc0 and newer, changes to that table are not saved to disk.

E.g. Go into **Preferences** -> **Expert**, click the **+** button beneath the table, and put in **tcp.analysis.duplicate_ack** for the **Field Name** and leave the **Severity** set to **Error**.  Choose OK, then exit out of Wireshark and relaunch it, return to **Preferences** > **Expert**, and the added row will have disappeared, where it would be expected to have been retained (as it was prior to this commit).

(I haven't tested with other UATs to see if it's a broader problem than this...)
This should be fixed with https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22069
mentioned in issue #20785
Sorry, I was traveling. I will discuss with the author and get back to you.

The UX for this feature is not good:
1. It's not easy to understand how this feature should work. It's no documentation and no examples what to expect.
2. When enabling aggregation view after the capture started all packets captured until this point is shown in the packet list but new packets are not added (no aggregation fields configured). Only the first line in the packet list is updated and during a live capture it's almost impossible to scroll back to the first line. It's not easy to understand which packets are shown in the list and which packets are not shown (and which packets are aggregated).
3. When selecting a packet the UI "jumps around" and it's not easy to expand subtrees or look at values.
4. The `aggregation` button in the toolbar is blurry on high resolution displays. This does not look good together with our other buttons. I don't think this icon reflects how the feature works, and the tooltip "Aggregation View" does not help without reading some documentation.
5. The `aggregation` button is documented to be in the toolbar, but is not visible until enabled in preferences. None of the other buttons behave like this.
6. Block turning off "Enable Aggregation View for real-time capturing" when the toolbar button is active is not user friendly. It should be possible to turn this off regardless of the toolbar button state.
7. The wsug `ws-main-toolbar.png` has changed from high resolution to low resolution.
8. After changing the aggregation fields during a live capture, and in some cases when enabling the aggregation view, a warning message is shown.

![Screenshot_2025-10-22_at_09.47.28](/uploads/e9851afc96e412d63ca09dd83c613146/Screenshot_2025-10-22_at_09.47.28.png)

9. When switching between profiles the aggregated view is sometimes ON sometimes OFF even if the profile does not have this enabled.

You are absolutely correct. We are looking into this. While testing, we also found a few things to improve concerning different profiles.

P.S. The preference -\> expert is also not very clear. ;-)
